attrs.title: MolMiner: Towards Controllable, 3D-Aware, Fragment-Based Molecular Design
attrs.research_question: 提出MolMiner，一种基于片段、几何感知且顺序无关的自回归模型，用于支持12个理化性质的高维条件控制分子设计。
attrs.why_hard: 现有自回归模型通常依赖固定的展开顺序，且很少在生成过程中整合动态几何信息，导致泛化能力受限。
attrs.name: MolMiner: Towards Controllable, 3D-Aware, Fragment-Based Molecular Design
attrs.label: MolMiner: Towards Controllable, 3D-Aware, Fragment-Based Molecular Design
attrs.abstract: We introduce MolMiner, a fragment-based, geometry-aware, and order-agnostic autoregressive model for molecular design. MolMiner supports high-dimensional conditional control over twelve physicochemical and structural properties from partial specifications, constructs molecules via symmetry-aware fragment attachments, and conditions each generation step on force-field-relaxed three-dimensional geometry of the partial structure. Conditional control emerges without auxiliary property losses. On targeted property windows, conditioning lifts hit rates by up to 5.25× over unconditional generation and 3.5× over the training distribution itself — overriding the model’s intrinsic biases — at the cost of a small reduction in unconditional distributional fidelity. MolMiner unifies dynamic geometry, symmetry handling, order-agnostic generation, and scalable multi-property conditioning within a single framework.

nodes.label: SO3LR Tauri: Generally Applicable Force Fields for Reactive (Bio)Molecular Simul

attrs.title: SO3LR Tauri: Generally Applicable Force Fields for Reactive (Bio)Molecular Simulations Covering the Periodic Table
attrs.research_question: 开发覆盖周期表85种元素、具备量子力学精度的通用机器学习力场，用于反应性生物分子模拟。
attrs.why_hard: 经典力场需针对每类生物分子单独拟合参数，且独立开发的参数集未设计为协同使用，难以统一描述所有分子类别。
attrs.name: SO3LR Tauri: Generally Applicable Force Fields for Reactive (Bio)Molecular Simul
attrs.label: SO3LR Tauri: Generally Applicable Force Fields for Reactive (Bio)Molecular Simul
attrs.abstract: Machine-learned force fields (MLFFs) aim to create a unified model that describes all major classes of (bio)molecules at quantum-mechanical accuracy. We present SO3LR Tauri, a family of MLFFs developed toward this goal, coupling a fast SO3krates network to explicit, physics-based interaction modules: pair-specific short-range repulsion, environment-dependent dispersion, and electrostatics, each improved beyond its original formulation. The models are trained on 148 million structures spanning 85 elements, drawn from several quantum-chemical datasets. Against coupled-cluster references, the models accurately reproduce nucleobase-pair and charged protein–ligand interactions, carbohydrate conformer ordering, and molecular dipoles. They also resolve the transition pathways of organic and enzymatic reactions. Dynamical simulations recover experimental densities of water and organic solvents, the hydration structure of mono- and divalent ions, the pKa values of amino-acid side chains, and the structure and dynamics of proteins, membranes, nucleic acids, glycoproteins, and metal-containing biomolecules, all without system-specific fitting. Released in three sizes, the models reach 0.7–3.2 µs/atom and scale to 27–84 million atoms on a single GPU. Much work remains to be done: achieving predictive accuracy for static and dynamic liquid properties, reaction barriers, coverage of chemical and conformational space, and the sampling and inference speed needed to describe biomolecular processes.

attrs.research_question: 开发一种抗体特异性逆折叠模型，在保持骨架结构不变的前提下生成序列并预测亲和力，以解决现有工具CDR序列恢复率低的问题。
attrs.flow_family: 结构基逆折叠/序列设计
attrs.why_hard: 现有逆折叠工具在CDR区域的序列恢复能力有限，且ProteinMPNN类工具存在链重排或插入等与抗体结构不兼容的特征。
attrs.name: AntiFold: Improved antibody structure-based design using inverse folding
attrs.label: AntiFold: Improved antibody structure-based design using inverse folding
attrs.abstract: Summary: The design and optimization of antibodies requires an intricate balance across multiple properties. Protein inverse folding models, capable of generating diverse sequences folding into the same structure, are promising tools for maintaining structural integrity during antibody design. Here, we present AntiFold, an antibody-specific inverse folding model, fine-tuned from ESM-IF1 on solved and predicted antibody structures. AntiFold outperforms existing inverse folding tools on sequence recovery across complementarity-determining regions, with designed sequences showing high structural similarity to their solved counterpart. It additionally achieves stronger correlations when predicting antibody-antigen binding affinity in a zero-shot manner, while performance is augmented further when including antigen information. AntiFold assigns low probabilities to mutations that disrupt antigen binding, synergizing with protein language model residue probabilities, and demonstrates promise for guiding antibody optimization while retaining structure-related properties.

attrs.research_question: 利用基于LLM的基础模型AMP-Designer，在有限数据下快速设计具有广谱抗菌活性、低毒性和稳定性的新型抗菌肽（AMPs）。

attrs.name: A foundation model approach to guide antimicrobial peptide design in the era of
attrs.label: A foundation model approach to guide antimicrobial peptide design in the era of
attrs.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown remarkable advancements in chemistry and biomedical research, acting as versatile foundation models for various tasks. We introduce AMP-Designer, an LLM-based approach for swiftly designing novel antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) with desired properties. Within 11 days, AMP-Designer achieved the de novo design of 18 AMPs with broad-spectrum activity against Gram-negative bacteria. In vitro validation revealed a 94.4% success rate, with two candidates demonstrating exceptional antibacterial efficacy, minimal hemotoxicity, stability in human plasma, and low potential to induce resistance, as evidenced by significant bacterial load reduction in murine lung infection experiments. The entire process, from design to validation, concluded in 48 days. AMP-Designer excels in creating AMPs targeting specific strains despite limited data availability, with a top candidate displaying a minimum inhibitory concentration of 2.0 μg/ml against Propionibacterium acnes. Integrating advanced machine learning techniques, AMP-Designer demonstrates remarkable efficiency, paving the way for innovative solutions to antibiotic resistance.
